title: Precept Ten - Non-Abusing the Three Treasures
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up the sixteenth Bodhisattva Precept, non-abusing the three treasures, through Nancy Mujo Baker's chapter and Bodhidharma's line about not raising a distinction between Buddhas and sentient beings. Nomon offers "rejoicing" as the positive side of the precept, then describes a grouchy, hunched work party at the temple under construction, where the tension eases by the next morning. Upstairs, the stored boxes of dusty, jumbled belongings become a heap of gold, the aspirations and generosity of thousands of people. Nomon suggests catching yourself being Buddha, the way a parent catches a child being good. The session ends with a monologue exercise in groups of three about times of closeness to the three treasures.
